finalText:
Migration finished. 12 files, 36 call sites converted to `db.execute({ sql, params })`, matching the shape used by the already-migrated files (e.g. `packages/billing/src/repo/coupon.js`). All 12 pass `node --check`.

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `repo/session.js` |
| billing | `service/couponService.js`, `repo/refund.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

Two things I deliberately left alone:

**`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** still calls `db.query`. Its header says the file is a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade, and local edits are silently lost — so patching it there would be reverted on the next bump. Since `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major drops `query` entirely, this needs a real fix rather than an in-place edit: either upgrade legacy-orm to a version on the new API, or wrap the adapter locally (a thin module that shims `query` → `execute` and passes that to the vendored code). Worth deciding before the driver bump, since it will break at runtime, not at build.

**`cache.query(...)`** appears in ~20 repo files. That's `lib/cache.js`, an unrelated API — not part of this migration.

`lib/db.js` still exports `query` with its `@deprecated` tag. Now that the only remaining caller is vendored, you could delete it to hard-fail any regression — say the word and I'll do that, though it will break the vendor adapter immediately.
